A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LightRetriever and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Their content can be reliably matched despite reformatting, renumbering, and additions.

before.justification: v4 reports original BeIR and CMTEB retrieval results, speed measurements, architectural ablations, and vector-truncation experiments.

after.justification: v5 retains these empirical results and adds CoIR and BRIGHT evaluations, additional comparisons, and handcrafted ranking cases.

M1.justification: Token caching and averaging, sparse token-count queries, LLM document encoding, losses, and optimization procedures are retained. Renaming the query 'MLP' to 'Embedding Bag' clarifies the existing implementation. The last-token pooling description remains consistent with the retained EOS-terminated input construction.

E1.justification: Appendix A.10 adds CoIR code retrieval and BRIGHT reasoning-intensive retrieval across three existing backbones. These introduce substantially different task requirements beyond the retained BeIR and CMTEB evaluations. The training collection remains unchanged.

E2.justification: v5 adds USTAD and SPLADE-v3 comparisons and includes BGE-large on BRIGHT. Table 1 adds Full-Llama3b and incorporates the previously ablated one-layer Llama8b, while dropping Qwen rows. Separate BGE-m3 dense/sparse rows disappear from Table 2, but their detailed appendix scores remain. These are targeted changes around the retained full-symmetric comparisons.

E3.justification: v5 extends timing comparisons to additional query-model configurations, introduces eight-category BeIR aggregation with retention ratios, and adds three handcrafted two-document ranking tests. Existing training budgets, data splits, retrieval metrics, and the main speed-test workload remain unchanged. Detailed protocols for the new CoIR and BRIGHT evaluations are not supplied.

E4.justification: New analyses examine task-category differences, compositional semantics, negation, and a technical-query failure (Table 3 and Appendix A.3). Appendix A.4 extends truncation analysis to query-embedding serving memory. Existing symmetry, one-layer, dense/sparse, and auxiliary-KL ablations remain, despite moves and renumbering.

E5.justification: v5 Table 1 introduces significance markers stating p <= 0.01 for encoding speed and throughput; v4 has no corresponding statistical reporting. The test procedure and repeated-run counts are unspecified, so this establishes new significance reporting without establishing additional runs.

E6.justification: Substantial new entries cover comparator scores, timings, cases, memory costs, and CoIR/BRIGHT results; LightRetriever-Qwen2.5-7B reports 49.0 and 11.6 nDCG@10 on the latter benchmarks. Figure 6 revises untruncated hybrid endpoints from 53.5/60.5 to 54.4/63.0 on BeIR/CMTEB-R, aligning them with retained main-table scores. These are reporting revisions, not demonstrated method improvements.

T1.justification: The retrieval objectives, representation equations, KL formulation, causal-mask definition, aggregation derivation, and Algorithm 1 retain their mathematical substance. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The central architecture, speedup, and approximately 95% performance-retention claims persist. The introduction adds an explicit claim about preserving semantic understanding through document-side modeling. The conclusion replaces its H800 and 20x CPU-speedup statement with A800 and 10x end-to-end throughput claims consistent with the abstract.

C2.justification: v4 describes domain-specific degradation as tolerable and mainly limits its scope regarding non-LLM architectures. v5 explicitly identifies complex-query, code, and reasoning-intensive retrieval as unsuitable applications, supported by new evaluations and a failure case. It also adds explanations involving document-side semantic capacity, lexical distractions, and memory-constrained deployment.

D1.justification: v5 newly reports approximately 15 hours of Llama8b training and under 20 seconds of caching on eight H800 GPUs, plus Float16 embedding memory requirements. Code changes from 'will be available' to 'is available.' Direct Sentence Transformers data and tDRO implementation links are removed, although the sources remain named.

R1.justification: v5 adds references for SPLADE-v3, CoIR, BRIGHT, and Mackenzie et al.'s SPLADE representation analysis, using the latter to motivate document-side semantic modeling. It removes the TREC 2019 overview, Tantivy, and Sentence Transformers data references. The broader positioning against symmetric and distilled retrievers remains stable.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites clarify embedding terminology, expand interpretation, and move the one-layer comparison into the main results. Category analysis and appendix subsections are added, and citations switch to author-year style. The overall introduction–algorithm–experiments–ablations–conclusion structure remains intact.

P2.justification: The visual presentation expands substantially with category, colored case-study, memory-tradeoff, CoIR, and BRIGHT tables. Speed and ablation tables are reorganized, Figure 6 curves are revised, and the ICLR format changes headers, typography, and placement throughout. The architecture diagrams and other existing figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: v5 improves applicability guidance through CoIR/BRIGHT evaluations and explicit failure conditions, while additional baselines, caching and memory costs, and corrected Figure 6 values improve assessment of the efficiency tradeoff. The gains are limited by insufficiently documented new-benchmark protocols, absent matched full-symmetric controls on those benchmarks, and an unexplained speed-significance test. Some direct reproducibility links are also lost.
